thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired for service=runtime-inference-latency (alert: p99 > 4500ms, window=3m). Paging primary on-call.

alice: ack. I'm on-call, looking at grafana now.

mike: grabbing quick checks — region breakdown?

sara: eu-west looks worst: p95 ~1.2s -> 2.8s, p99 ~6.4s. us-east minor bump. KV cache evictions spiked ~00:12UTC.

elena: any recent rollout? I see a quantization roll-forward at 00:05, but it was for model-x-lite (canary).

james: oh weird — canary should be isolated. logs show a surge of large-batch requests from a single client id around 00:10.

alice: running runbook step1 (check autoscaler, queue depth, hotkeys).

alice: autoscaler shows no recent scale events; queue depth 3x normal on inference-sidecar; preemptions low.

mike: can we divert traffic away from model-x (heavy) to model-x-ml (low-latency) as temporary fallback?

sara: agree. also try warming kvcache for top hotkeys.

elena: initiating route tweak (canary shift) — will do 10% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics look good.

james: posting the route update snippet I'm using:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/route/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"service":"runtime-inference","from":"model-x","to":"model-x-ml","weight":50}'
```

alice: applied 10% now.

incident-bot: :information_source: After 5m with no ACK from escalation target, page auto-escalated to secondary on-call.

mike: ack (secondary). I see p99 trending down in eu-west from 6.4s -> 3.1s after 10% shift.

sara: starting kvcache prewarm for top-50 prefixes. command:

```
kubectl exec -it prewarm-job -- /bin/bash -c "python prewarm.py --prefix-file /tmp/top50.txt"
```

elena: bumping dedicated pool by +2 GPUs via infra-console (temp). ETA ~3m to be available.

james: client-request surge looks like a retry storm from partner-integrator Beta; reached out via #partner-ops.

alice: summary of mitigations so far: 1) 10% traffic divert -> observed p99 drop; 2) kvcache prewarm launched; 3) +2 GPU reserve requested; 4) monitoring for error rates and latency tail.

mike: can we enable a short-term circuit breaker for very large batch sizes from that client id? suggested rule: reject > 4k tokens or batch-size > 32.

sara: putting a temporary filter in edge: added rule to drop abusive batch requests. log shows now the offending client at 0.1% of traffic.

alice: after raising to 50% route shift and cache warm, eu-west p99 ~720ms, p95 ~420ms. still above target but under control.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager acknowledged by alice and mike; incident status: mitigation in progress. Next auto-escalation in 15m if SLO not recovered.

elena: dedicated GPUs live. autoscaler didn't kick but infra manual add is in. rebalancing traffic to new nodes.

james: partner replied — they pushed a fix to back off retries. they will throttle to 1 req/s per key for next hour.

mike: good. I'll keep an eye on p99 and error budget burn rate. current SLO burn: 3.8% over the hour window (target <1%).

sara: starting a brief customer-impact check: dev-sandboxes and a handful of EU customers saw degraded tail latency and 502s. No mass data loss.

alice: plan: hold current mitigations for 30m, then slowly roll traffic back to model-x while monitoring. owners: alice (oncall) + sara (runtime). Postmortem owner: sara.

mike: can we also add an alert to detect retry storms (pattern: many identical payloads from same client) to prevent recurrence?

sara: yes — will add a detector and a short playbook. follow-up task in #triage: create autotune for batch-size throttling.

alice: thanks team. I'll update ops-bridge and set follow-up meeting at 10:30 UTC. current status: mitigated, partial customer impact, recovery in progress.

james: noted. moving to watch. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :tada: Alert resolved (p99 back under 800ms for 10m). Closing page thread.
